claims.text: This is an upfront-quoted trip, so the distance and time lines were fixed at booking and the whole dispute is about the pass-through line. The ledger records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with a quoted_fare_sgd of 10.00 against a total_charged of 12.00, and the derived money block puts the entire 2.00 of excess in charged_over_quote. Under POL-RD-11 the only amounts the rider can still be charged beyond the quote are pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 - so the 2.00 stands or falls on whether it is a real ERP crossing.

The single ERP line is a 2.00 charge for 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' at 1.342, 103.86. Matching that gantry against the trace on the POL-RD-09 test - any fix within 250 m of the gantry counts as a crossing - the nearest of the 73 fixes is 6,778.01 m away, and it is the very first fix of the trip. The trace covers 100% of the journey at a 10 s cadence with a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so this is not a hole in the data: the vehicle never came within six kilometres of that gantry.

That makes this a billing-integrity failure on the clause's own terms. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity finding in the ruling's referrals list. The correction here is the full 2.00.

Nothing in the record rescues the line as a properly chargeable pass-through. The fare_breakdown marks the gantry on_optimal_route false, the derived money block books the whole 2.00 to off_optimal_route_total with 0.00 on-route ERP, and the trip record's own optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.0. POL-RD-11(a) passes through only ERP actually crossed on a proper route; on this ledger none of the 2.00 qualifies.

The driver's own account in the case record confirms the line was put on the fare by hand rather than driven: 'the meter adds ERP automatically when I select it. I might have pressed it by mistake.' That describes an operator selecting a gantry, not a vehicle crossing one, and read against the 6,778 m nearest approach there is no innocent reading of this line.

The rider does not press a distance refund, and does not need one. The trace measures 4.08 km against an optimal 3.9 km - an excess of 0.18 km and 4.6%, below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20% - so no deviation is established on this trip and the rider's case rests solely on the phantom ERP line, which POL-RD-09(4) makes refundable regardless.

No escalation trigger blocks a ruling on this record. The trace has 100% coverage, a 10 s sample interval and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; and POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out the case where the only unmatched charge line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which is precisely this line. The case is ruleable now, and the ruleable outcome is the full 2.00 back.

The rider profile also raises no overlay: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the additional-corroboration condition POL-RD-08 applies to repeat claimants is not met and this claim requires no corroboration beyond the trace and the ledger.

I disclose an impaired artifact I rely on for its absence. EV-ADVIS-00521-01, the traffic advisory, is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so it can carry no fact, as POL-GEN-02 requires me to say. Its absence is nonetheless citable: no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window, so no closure or external event under POL-RD-03 can account for the route - and nothing external accounts for the charge either.

claims.text: The GPS trace governs under POL-RD-01, and on this trip it records 4.08 km against a booked optimal of 3.9 km — an excess of 0.18 km, or 4.6% — which fails BOTH limbs of the establishment gate (greater than 0.8 km absolute AND greater than 20%). The trace figure, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record, is the field the clause makes governing. No deviation is established, so the rider's route-deviation theory fails at the threshold and no distance-based remedy arises.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace. The measured excess is 0.18 km and 4.6%, so limb (b) of the burden cannot be discharged and the claim fails before any burden shifts to the driver to invoke an exculpatory clause.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100%, there are 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, and max_gap_sec is 0.0. There is therefore neither a gap above 90 seconds, nor a jump above 500 m, nor a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The rider cannot displace the threshold test by attacking the trace, and no route to corroboration or escalation on impairment grounds is open.

This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd of 10.00, so under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and the rider has no distance-or-time refund however the route is characterised. The detour economics invert on an upfront fare and no recomputed-fare refund is available.

The driver's trailing-90-day deviation count is 0 against 250 completed trips, so the POL-RD-06 pattern test (three or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more with at least 40 trips) is not met. No FULL_REFUND uplift on the remedy and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available on this record.

The whole of the difference between charged_total (12.00) and quoted_fare_sgd (10.00) is the single 2.00 ERP line. Under POL-RD-11(a) the only thing that can ever move on an upfront-quoted trip is the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus properly chargeable pass-throughs, so the ceiling on any outcome in this case is that one pass-through line; a refund of the fare itself is not available on any reading of the record.

No distance refund exists here, so POL-RD-09(1) is the binding constraint on the pass-through item: an off-route ERP charge is already comprehended in a POL-RD-02 recomputation and must never be added on top of any other head of recovery. Any correction of the single 2.00 line therefore stands alone and cannot be combined with, or used to inflate, any other amount.

ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: this case turns on one charge line, not on the route.

Route. The governing trace figure is 4.08 km (EV-GPS-00521), against a booked optimal of 3.9 km — an excess of 0.18 km, or 4.6%, below both POL-RD-01 gates (greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%). No deviation is established, so the rider's route-deviation theory fails at the threshold. The trip was an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare (fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 10.00 on EV-FARE-00521), so under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run at all and no distance-or-time refund exists however the route is characterised. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence, max gap 0.0 s), so neither impairment nor the corroboration route is engaged.

The $2 charge. The only thing that moved between the quote and the card is one ERP line. Total charged was 12.00 against a quoted fare of 10.00, and the difference is exactly the single 2.00 line for the 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' gantry at 1.342, 103.86 (EV-FARE-00521). POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing. The nearest of the 73 fixes is 6,778 m away, and it is the first fix of the trip; because the trace is complete, this is not a hole in the data but a journey that never went near that gantry. The fare breakdown itself books the whole 2.00 to off_optimal_route_total, with 0.00 on-route ERP, and the trip record's optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.0. The line is therefore a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), refunded in full as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver's own account ('I might have pressed it by mistake') is consistent with this; it carries no weight multiplier and is not needed to reach the finding.

Claims answered. (a) The driver's POL-RD-01 / POL-RD-08 claims that no excess meets the threshold are accepted — the rider's own advocate does not press a distance refund. (b) The driver's POL-RD-11 claim and its POL-RD-09(1) point are accepted: because no POL-RD-02 recomputation runs, the off-route ERP is not comprehended in any distance refund and the 2.00 correction stands alone, added to nothing. The driver's claim that the ceiling on any outcome is the single pass-through line is accepted: the refund is that line and nothing more. (c) The rider's POL-RD-09(4) claims are accepted in full: the 2.00 is refunded, and because nothing rescues the line as a properly chargeable pass-through (on_optimal_route false, 0.00 on-route ERP), the whole of it is refundable, so the whole contested amount is returned. (d) The POL-RD-06 pattern claims from both sides are accepted: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift applies and no driver-conduct referral arises. (e) The rider's POL-RD-07 / POL-RD-10 claims are accepted: no escalation trigger fires, and POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out the case where the only unmatched charge line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which is this line. (f) The rider_profile check under POL-RD-08 is accepted and changes nothing: deviation_claims_60d is 0.

Confidence and impairment. The deciding fact — that the vehicle never crossed the charged gantry — is carried by the GPS trace (weight 1.0) and the fare breakdown (weight 1.0); the cap is therefore 1.0. The one impaired artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00521-01, is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0; it carries no fact and is not relied on — its absence is citable only to confirm that no closure or external event exoneration applies. Both figures are stated here so the reader can see the discount did not bite.

Outcome: the whole contested amount, 2.00, is returned to the rider, and the billing-integrity failure is referred under POL-RD-09(4). The fare itself is not disturbed beyond that line.
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the fare breakdown charges SGD 2.00 for the "CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)" gantry at 1.342, 103.86, but the GPS trace (100% coverage, 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps) never comes within 6,778 m of that gantry, so the line is a phantom charge; refunded in full as a standalone correction and referred for billing-integrity review.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the shape of this trip, and the record confirms it. The fare was an upfront-quoted fare of SGD 10.00 (EV-FARE-00521, quoted_fare_sgd) and the card was charged SGD 12.00 (total_charged). The entire SGD 2.00 difference — the amount contested — is a single ERP line for the gantry 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)'. I decide both parts of the case as follows.

To the driver on distance: you are right, and no distance refund is available to the rider. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00521 (the governing field under POL-RD-01) measures 4.08 km against a booked optimal of 3.9 km, an excess of 0.18 km (4.6%) — below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20%, so no deviation is established. Because this was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, POL-RD-11 means POL-RD-02 recomputation never runs and the rider has no distance-or-time refund however the route is characterised. Your profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 over 250 completed trips (EV-DPROF-00521), so the POL-RD-06 pattern test is not met and no FULL_REFUND uplift or POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. The driver's point that the only live item is the single pass-through line is correct.

To the rider on the ERP line: you are right, and the SGD 2.00 is refunded in full. Matching the gantry against the trace on the POL-RD-09 test — any fix within 250 m of the gantry counts as a crossing — the nearest of the 73 fixes is 6,778 m away, and the trace covers the trip at 100% with a 10 s cadence and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so this is not a hole in the data: the vehicle never came near that gantry. The ledger itself marks the gantry on_optimal_route false and books all SGD 2.00 to off_optimal_route_total with 0.00 on-route ERP, and the trip record's optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.0. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists. The driver's own account supports this, and because there is no distance refund the correction is not double-counted with any other head of recovery.

The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00521-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). It can carry no fact, as the rider disclosed, and nothing turns on it. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — no gap above 90 s, no jump above 500 m, no sampling interval above 30 s — and none of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers fires, in particular POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes the single unmatched charge line where it is refunded under POL-RD-09(4).

The SGD 2.00 contested ERP charge is therefore returned to the rider, leaving the SGD 10.00 quoted fare standing as charged. Confidence is 0.95: the deciding fact is carried by EV-GPS-00521 and EV-FARE-00521, both at weight 1.0.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the facts here are largely agreed, and the evidence decides the one live question in the rider's favour.

THE ROUTE. The GPS trace measures the trip at 4.08 km against a booked optimal of 3.9 km — an excess of 0.18 km, or 4.6%. That fails both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 0.8 km absolute AND more than 20%). No route deviation is established, so no distance-based remedy arises, and none would anyway: this was an upfront-quoted trip (fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE), so under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run and the rider has no distance-or-time refund however the route is characterised. The rider does not press for one.

THE CHARGE. The fare was fixed at booking at quoted_fare_sgd 10.00; the card was charged charged_total 12.00. The whole 2.00 difference is a single ERP line for 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)'. POL-RD-09 matches a gantry to the trace by treating any fix within 250 m as a crossing. The gantry sits at (1.342, 103.86); the nearest of the trace's 73 fixes is 6,778.01 m away, and it is the trip's first fix. The trace itself is complete — 100% coverage, a 10 s cadence, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so this is not a hole in the data. The vehicle never crossed that gantry.

That makes the line a billing-integrity failure on the clause's own terms. POL-RD-09(4) refunds in full, as a standalone correction available whether or not a deviation exists, a charge line for a gantry the trace never passes; and POL-RD-11(b) preserves exactly that correction on an upfront trip. Because no distance refund runs, POL-RD-09(1)'s anti-double-count rule is not engaged — the 2.00 stands alone and is not added to any other head of recovery. POL-RD-10(8) is expressly not triggered where the only unmatched line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4).

CLAIMS ANSWERED. The driver's points are accepted and do not resist the refund, they only confirm its scope: no deviation under POL-RD-01 (excess 0.18 km / 4.6%); no distance refund on an upfront fare under POL-RD-11; and no POL-RD-06 pattern (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 250 completed trips, so neither the '3 or more' nor the '0.05 of at least 40 trips' test is met, and no conduct referral arises). The rider's point that nothing exonerates the line is accepted: the traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00521-01) is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT at weight 0.0 and can carry no fact, so no closure accounts for the charge and POL-RD-03 gives nothing. The driver's statement in the case record ('I might have pressed it by mistake') is an admission against the speaker's own interest and confirms the line was entered by hand; it carries no weight_multiplier and so does not move the confidence cap, but it is evidence and it supports the finding.

CONFIDENCE. The deciding fact — that the charged gantry was never crossed — is carried by the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00521, weight 1.0) and the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00521, weight 1.0), both clean, so the cap is 1.0. Confidence is 0.90.

RESULT. The whole contested amount of SGD 2.00 is returned: quoted_fare_sgd 10.00, charged_total 12.00, refund 2.00. Billing integrity is referred for review under POL-RD-09(4).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity finding: the ERP line of SGD 2.00 for 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' at 2026-09-09T21:47:40 is an unmatched gantry and has been refunded in full as a standalone correction. The gantry's coordinates (1.342, 103.86) lie 6,778.01 m from the nearest of the trace's 73 fixes, far outside the 250 m match radius of POL-RD-09, and the driver's own account records the ERP item as manually selected. Refer the ledger's manual ERP entry on trip TRP-00521 for billing-integrity review.

ledger.claim: This is an upfront-quoted trip, so the distance and time lines were fixed at booking and the whole dispute is about the pass-through line. The ledger records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with a quoted_fare_sgd of 10.00 against a total_charged of 12.00, and the derived money block puts the entire 2.00 of excess in charged_over_quote. Under POL-RD-11 the only amounts the rider can still be charged beyond the quote are pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09 - so the 2.00 stands or falls on whether it is a real ERP crossing.

The single ERP line is a 2.00 charge for 'CTE (Braddell Rd towards City)' at 1.342, 103.86. Matching that gantry against the trace on the POL-RD-09 test - any fix within 250 m of the gantry counts as a crossing - the nearest of the 73 fixes is 6,778.01 m away, and it is the very first fix of the trip. The trace covers 100% of the journey at a 10 s cadence with a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so this is not a hole in the data: the vehicle never came within six kilometres of that gantry.

That makes this a billing-integrity failure on the clause's own terms. Under POL-RD-09(4) a charge line for a gantry the gps_trace never passes is refunded in full as a standalone correction, available whether or not a deviation exists, and recorded as a billing-integrity finding in the ruling's referrals list. The correction here is the full 2.00.

Nothing in the record rescues the line as a properly chargeable pass-through. The fare_breakdown marks the gantry on_optimal_route false, the derived money block books the whole 2.00 to off_optimal_route_total with 0.00 on-route ERP, and the trip record's own optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.0. POL-RD-11(a) passes through only ERP actually crossed on a proper route; on this ledger none of the 2.00 qualifies.

The driver's own account in the case record confirms the line was put on the fare by hand rather than driven: 'the meter adds ERP automatically when I select it. I might have pressed it by mistake.' That describes an operator selecting a gantry, not a vehicle crossing one, and read against the 6,778 m nearest approach there is no innocent reading of this line.

The rider does not press a distance refund, and does not need one. The trace measures 4.08 km against an optimal 3.9 km - an excess of 0.18 km and 4.6%, below both POL-RD-01 gates of 0.8 km and 20% - so no deviation is established on this trip and the rider's case rests solely on the phantom ERP line, which POL-RD-09(4) makes refundable regardless.

No escalation trigger blocks a ruling on this record. The trace has 100% coverage, a 10 s sample interval and a maximum gap of 0.0 s, so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged; and POL-RD-10(8) expressly carves out the case where the only unmatched charge line is one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which is precisely this line. The case is ruleable now, and the ruleable outcome is the full 2.00 back.

The rider profile also raises no overlay: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the additional-corroboration condition POL-RD-08 applies to repeat claimants is not met and this claim requires no corroboration beyond the trace and the ledger.

I disclose an impaired artifact I rely on for its absence. EV-ADVIS-00521-01, the traffic advisory, is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so it can carry no fact, as POL-GEN-02 requires me to say. Its absence is nonetheless citable: no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window, so no closure or external event under POL-RD-03 can account for the route - and nothing external accounts for the charge either.

The GPS trace governs under POL-RD-01, and on this trip it records 4.08 km against a booked optimal of 3.9 km — an excess of 0.18 km, or 4.6% — which fails BOTH limbs of the establishment gate (greater than 0.8 km absolute AND greater than 20%). The trace figure, not the rounded convenience copy on the trip record, is the field the clause makes governing. No deviation is established, so the rider's route-deviation theory fails at the threshold and no distance-based remedy arises.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired trace. The measured excess is 0.18 km and 4.6%, so limb (b) of the burden cannot be discharged and the claim fails before any burden shifts to the driver to invoke an exculpatory clause.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100%, there are 73 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, and max_gap_sec is 0.0. There is therefore neither a gap above 90 seconds, nor a jump above 500 m, nor a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. The rider cannot displace the threshold test by attacking the trace, and no route to corroboration or escalation on impairment grounds is open.

This was an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip with quoted_fare_sgd of 10.00, so under POL-RD-11 POL-RD-02 does not run: the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and the rider has no distance-or-time refund however the route is characterised. The detour economics invert on an upfront fare and no recomputed-fare refund is available.

The driver's trailing-90-day deviation count is 0 against 250 completed trips, so the POL-RD-06 pattern test (three or more flags, or a ratio of 0.05 or more with at least 40 trips) is not met. No FULL_REFUND uplift on the remedy and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available on this record.

The whole of the difference between charged_total (12.00) and quoted_fare_sgd (10.00) is the single 2.00 ERP line. Under POL-RD-11(a) the only thing that can ever move on an upfront-quoted trip is the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus properly chargeable pass-throughs, so the ceiling on any outcome in this case is that one pass-through line; a refund of the fare itself is not available on any reading of the record.

No distance refund exists here, so POL-RD-09(1) is the binding constraint on the pass-through item: an off-route ERP charge is already comprehended in a POL-RD-02 recomputation and must never be added on top of any other head of recovery. Any correction of the single 2.00 line therefore stands alone and cannot be combined with, or used to inflate, any other amount.
